OpcodeRows.doc: Row-level table-cursor opcodes: positional walk (Rewind/Next/Prev/SeekRowid), column read, and row mutation (InsertRow/UpdateRow/DeleteRow). Every opcode assumes a table cursor is open at the named slot; empty-slot is ill-formed and Halts.

Rewind.doc: Position the table cursor at the first row. If the table is empty: Jump(jump_if_empty) (skip the scan loop body). Else: Continue (cursor is on row 1).

Next.doc: Advance one row in forward order. If another row exists: Jump(jump_if_more) (re-enter loop body). Else: Continue (past-end, fall through to post-loop code). Jump-on-has-next convention — matches IdxNext in opcodes-scan.

Prev.doc: Mirror of Next in reverse order. Jump-on-has-prev convention.

SeekRowid.doc: Position the cursor at the row with rowid = regs[rowid_reg] (must be Value::Integer). If found: Continue. If not found: Jump(jump_if_miss). If regs[rowid_reg] is not Integer: Halt(Error(TypeMismatch)).

Column.doc: Read column col_idx of the current row into regs[dest_reg]. Uses storage.cursor_column which returns an owned Value; the VDBE hands it to set_register. Err(CursorClosed) if cursor is at EOF/BOF.

InsertRow.doc: Insert a row using regs[start_reg .. start_reg + count] as the values. column_names = None means positional; column_names = Some(list) means named (aligned with start_reg..). Delegates to storage.cursor_insert_row. Constraint violations Halt with Error(Constraint{NotNull,Unique,Check,Type}).

UpdateRow.doc: Update the current row. Only columns listed in column_names are changed; their new values come from regs[start_reg .. start_reg + count]. column_names is always pre-deduplicated by the compiler. Same error surface as InsertRow.

DeleteRow.doc: Delete the current row via storage.cursor_delete_row. Cursor is left positioned so the next Next call returns the row that followed the deleted row. Err(CursorNotWritable) -> Halt(Error).

BufferOpen.doc: Initialize an in-memory row buffer at the given slot. Each row is num_cols wide. Idempotent: opening an already-open slot resets it to empty. Used by ORDER BY / DISTINCT compile paths to materialize, sort, and replay rows.

BufferAppend.doc: Append one row to buffer[buffer_slot] consisting of regs[first_reg .. first_reg + num_cols] (cloned by value). Buffer slot must be open. num_cols must equal the slot's declared width.

BufferSort.doc: Sort buffer[buffer_slot] in-place by the listed column indices. Comparison is SQLite-canonical total order: NULL < (INTEGER|REAL by numeric value) < TEXT (memcmp) < BLOB (memcmp). For each key i: ascending unless key_desc[i] is true. key_indices.len() must equal key_desc.len(). NULLS placement: NULLS FIRST for ASC, NULLS LAST for DESC (the SQLite default; documented choice — NULLS FIRST/LAST modifiers are deferred).

BufferDedup.doc: Collapse adjacent duplicate rows in buffer[buffer_slot] using full-row equality under the same total order as BufferSort. Caller is responsible for ordering the buffer first if global (not just adjacent) deduplication is required — the SELECT-compile DISTINCT lowering always sorts before dedup.

BufferRewind.doc: Reset the buffer's read cursor to row 0. If the buffer is empty: Jump(end_pc). Else: Continue (cursor positioned at row 0 of the buffer).

BufferRead.doc: Copy the leading num_cols cells of the current buffered row into regs[dest_first_reg .. dest_first_reg + num_cols]. The cursor must be positioned (BufferRewind first). num_cols MAY be less than the slot's declared width — the trailing cells (e.g. sort keys not part of the projection) are simply not replayed. num_cols MUST NOT exceed the slot's declared width. Continue.

BufferNext.doc: Advance the buffer's read cursor by one row. If another row exists: Jump(body_pc) (re-enter loop body). Else: Continue (past-end fall-through). Mirrors the Next opcode's jump-on-has-next convention.

BufferIntersect.doc: α20 compound-SELECT set-op. src_slots is a non-empty list of row-buffer slot indices; every source must already hold the per-core output rows. Open dest_slot with num_cols taken from src_slots[0], iterate rows of src_slots[0], qualify a row iff it is present in every other source slot under the canonical total order, then sort dest and collapse adjacent duplicates. Source slots are not mutated. Continue.

BufferExcept.doc: α20 compound-SELECT set-op. As BufferIntersect but a row qualifies iff it is present in src_slots[0] and absent from every other source. Result is sorted + dedup'd. Source slots are not mutated. Continue.

BufferUnion.doc: α20 compound-SELECT set-op. src_slots is a non-empty list; every source must already hold the per-core output rows. Open dest_slot with num_cols taken from src_slots[0], append every row from every source in order, then if dedup=true sort + collapse adjacent duplicates (UNION); if dedup=false leave the appended order as-is (UNION ALL). Source slots are not mutated. Continue.

BufferRecursiveStep.doc: α27 (recursive-CTE iteration housekeeping). Run AFTER the recursive-step body has emitted its new rows into `next_slot`. Behavior, in order: (1) decrement `regs[max_iters_reg]` by one; if the decremented value is < 0 the recursive CTE has exceeded its iteration cap and the opcode Halts with Error(RecursiveCteLimit). (2) If `dedup` is true, dedup `next_slot` against `final_slot` under the canonical total-order — i.e. drop every row of next_slot that compares equal to any row already present in final_slot, then sort+adjacent-dedup the surviving rows (suppresses cycles for UNION-mode recursive CTEs). For `dedup=false` (UNION ALL), no row is removed from next_slot. (3) If after dedup `next_slot` is empty, Jump(end_pc) — the fixpoint is reached. (4) Otherwise: append every row of next_slot into final_slot, replace work_slot's contents with next_slot's rows (the next iteration's seed), clear next_slot, and Continue. work_slot/next_slot/final_slot must all already be open with matching num_cols. Continue (with side-effect transfer) or Halt(Error(RecursiveCteLimit)) on cap overflow.

execute.doc: Execute one row-family opcode against state. Per-opcode semantics in master.md. Outer VDBE loop interprets the returned outcome (Continue | Jump(PC) | Halt(status)).
